what_its_for: Extended phenytoin is used to prevent and control seizures (epilepsy). It works by calming down abnormal electrical activity in the brain that causes seizures. It may also be used to prevent certain types of seizures that can happen after brain surgery.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or open it. You can take it with or without food, but try to take it the same way each time. Take it at the same time every day to keep a steady level of medicine in your body. If you take it once a day, take it at the same time each day. If you take it more than once a day, space your doses evenly throughout the day.
dosing: Your doctor will set your dose based on your weight, other medical conditions, and how your body responds to the medicine. A common starting adult dose is 100 mg taken 3 times a day, or 300 mg taken once a day. Do not change your dose on your own. Your doctor may need to do blood tests to make sure you are getting the right amount of medicine.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Missing doses can increase your risk of having a seizure. Call your doctor if you are not sure what to do.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol — it can make side effects worse and affect how well the medicine works. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking antacids at the same time as your phenytoin dose — they can make it harder for your body to absorb the medicine. Grapefruit and grapefruit juice may also affect this medicine, so ask your doctor or pharmacist if it is safe for you. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this could cause serious seizures.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have: a new or worsening seizure, signs of a serious skin reaction such as a rash, blistering, or peeling skin, swollen glands, fever, sore throat, unusual bruising or bleeding, yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems), confusion, slurred speech, or trouble walking, signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing, thoughts of hurting yourself or depression. Also call your doctor if you notice your gums are growing over your teeth (gum overgrowth), as this is a known side effect.
when_it_works: Extended phenytoin starts working in your body fairly quickly, but it may take several days to weeks for your doctor to find the right dose that works best for you. Do not stop taking it even if you feel well — seizure medicines work best when taken every day as prescribed. Regular blood tests will help your doctor make sure the medicine is at the right level in your body.
special_populations: Pregnancy: This medicine can harm an unborn baby. Talk to your doctor right away if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Do not stop taking it without medical guidance, as uncontrolled seizures can also be dangerous during pregnancy. Women of childbearing age should use effective birth control. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects such as confusion, dizziness, or falls, and may need a lower dose. Children: Dosing is based on weight and age — follow your child's doctor instructions carefully. Kidney or Liver disease: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have kidney or liver problems.
